title: Nash Existence For Finite Games
body_html:
Nash Existence For Finite Games

Every finite strategic game has a mixed equilibrium.
proof_html:
Sketch

MFoGT constructs Nash's continuous self-map $f$ on $$ \Delta=\prod_{i\in I}\Delta(S_i) $$ by increasing the weight of pure strategies whose payoff exceeds the current expected payoff. Brouwer's fixed point theorem gives $\sigma=f(\sigma)$. At such a fixed point, no player can have a pure strategy with strictly larger payoff than $g_i(\sigma)$; otherwise the normalization equation forces a contradiction for a strategy in the support. Hence $\sigma$ is a mixed Nash equilibrium.
